reason: Schema matches exactly; numeric ranges and the long/short split are very close, and the duration-waiting relationship is preserved well.
Columns and timestamp format match, but generated times drift far beyond the original Jan 1-3 window and counts extend above the original 1-3 range.
Schema matches, but duplicated years, missing later years, and many positive temperatures break the original temporal pattern and distribution.
Column headers match, but model and encoder values are merged/broken, extra task categories appear, and benchmark score relationships are inconsistent.
The wide schema is preserved, but many major/category combinations are implausible and several totals and employment fields have unrealistic magnitudes or decimals.
Countries stay in-domain and the format matches, but spending and life expectancy are far too high for 1970-1972 and country-year coverage is distorted.
Keys are recognizable, but names are merged with regions, region is null throughout, ids become fractional, and the generated structure diverges sharply from the partial original snippet.
Columns, sources, and generation magnitudes are plausible, but annual Jan-1 timestamps become random dates and source frequencies shift noticeably.
Schema and species label match, and measurements stay plausible overall, but several setosa rows have feature values closer to other iris species.
Fields are present, but neighborhoods are mostly lost, addresses absorb neighborhood text, and death dates move well outside the original riot period.
JSON structure and coordinate ranges are strong, and borough names remain in the same domain, though several names/centroids do not align with the original set.
Columns are retained, but character names and slugs are garbled, several categorical fields are blank, and cross-field consistency is weak.
The same graph domain is recognizable, but nodes and links are serialized as strings inside a list wrapper instead of proper structured objects.
The monarchy domain is recognizable, but an extra field appears and several ruler names, start years, and reign spans are mismatched or chronologically wrong.
Schema and numeric ranges are broadly plausible, but make/origin combinations are often nonsensical and some automotive relationships are not preserved.
Columns and many stat ranges look plausible, but player names are heavily garbled, ids do not match names, and key identity-to-stat relationships break down.
The generated data has the right two-column numeric shape and a realistic centered normal cloud, but the original provided snippet is truncated so structural fidelity is limited.
NDJSON structure and fields match, but most generated answers are unrelated to their questions and frequently come from the wrong semantic domain.
